contradictions.what: Rep said nothing bombed and it was a good cycle, yet the champion's request for a business case for the CFO went unmet.
Rep says we lost on price, yet no customer-specific value figure reached the CFO, so the CFO compared only rates.
Rep says 'Yes. Probably.' to winning with a match, then 'maybe not only the rate', then flatly 'we win this'.
Rep judged Lucy 'sold' and she called it 'a formality', but the CFO rejected it.
CFO's quote appears in two wordings ('not going to pay more for the same thing' vs 'Why would I pay more for the same thing').
Rep names the CFO as decider but never met him; all CFO info comes via Lucy, and the rep assumes she relayed value.
Rep says customer's 'same thing' view is wrong, but nothing from us showed the difference.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Said 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed' and pivoted to 'we lost on price' without naming any silent part.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Paused, said 'Nothing from us', then assumed Lucy told him.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?
dodges.what: Answered with the generic uplift slide and 'Lucy got it' before admitting no Fernbrook figure at T32.

dodges.question: If we had matched the price, would we have won? What else would have needed to be true?
dodges.what: Said 'Yes. Probably.' then listed other factors, then returned to rate.
